   101	
   102	## Goals
   103	
   104	- Remove all tracked machine-local checkout references and prevent recurrence
   105	  with a deterministic repository verification command.
   106	- Make tracked docs, specs, task lists, plans and root guidance portable across
   107	  clean checkouts without erasing useful repository-relative history.
   108	- Define and apply a canonical string-contract taxonomy to exported,
   109	  configured, persisted and provider-facing values.
   110	- Reuse owner-named schemas and schema-derived types instead of introducing
   111	  generic brand helpers, raw string mirrors or repeated defensive decoding.
   112	- Add only portable Effect lint rules that have a reliable static signal,
   113	  exact TaxKit scopes, accepted/rejected real-binary fixtures and a manageable
   114	  migration path.
   115	- Keep TaxKit-specific tax, decoder and route-transport rules separate from
   116	  domain-neutral Effect rules.
   117	- Add a production-only Knip graph for release-train packages,
   118	  `@taxkit/scripts` command entrypoints and `apps/api`.
   119	- Make the path and production-graph checks part of canonical root
   120	  verification.
   121	
   122	## Non-goals
   123	
   124	- Website identity, metadata, SEO, AEO, Open Graph or canonical page policy.
   125	- Design-system, route, browser, accessibility, performance or website
   126	  deployment work.
   127	- Replacing, redesigning or further hardening the current docs or web apps.
   128	- Adding the current docs or web apps to the production-only Knip graph in
   129	  this rollout.
   130	- Copying another repository's source, names, paths, deployment choices or
   131	  complete lint configuration.
   132	- Branding every string, creating a generic schema/brand factory or moving
   133	  owner-specific schemas into a shared bucket.
   134	- Replacing TaxKit's stricter decoder placement or direct route-consumer
   135	  contracts.
   136	- npm publication, repository versioning, release tags or automated release
   137	  pull requests.
   138	
   139	## Ownership and Boundaries
   140	
   141	- Root configuration owns canonical verification scripts and Knip entrypoint
   142	  selection.
   143	- `@taxkit/scripts` owns the cross-repository path policy, its schema-backed
   144	  findings, typed failures, test substitution and executable runtime. It must
   145	  remain a focused repository check rather than becoming a generic file-scan
   146	  framework.
   147	- Each domain, API, SDK, rule, config or automation owner continues to own its
   148	  string schemas and derived types. This spec defines selection policy, not a
   149	  new central schema package.
   150	- `tools/oxlint/effect-rules.js` owns domain-neutral Effect rules and
   151	  `tools/oxlint/taxkit-rules.js` retains tax, decoder and route-transport
   152	  policy. `oxlint.config.ts` owns exact enabled scopes and boundary allowlists.
   153	- The dedicated production Knip configuration owns production reachability
   154	  for release packages, repository commands and `apps/api`. It does not change
   155	  package exports or runtime ownership.
   156	
   157	All implementation must follow
   158	[Effect services](../architecture/effect-services.md),
   159	[Package ownership](../architecture/package-ownership.md),
   160	[Configuration](../architecture/configuration.md),
   161	[Testing and quality](../architecture/testing-and-quality.md) and
   162	[Code patterns](../standards/code-patterns.md).
   163	
   164	## Proposed Approach
   165	
   166	### 1. Repository path hygiene
   167	
   168	Replace machine-local checkout paths with repository-relative links,
   169	repository identities, pinned external references or concise historical
   170	descriptions. Historical plans remain useful, but their evidence must not
   171	require a particular username, home directory or checkout layout.
   172	
   173	Add one `@taxkit/scripts` command that inventories tracked text, rejects
   174	machine-local home and checkout references, reports schema-backed file/line
   175	findings and exits non-zero when violations exist. Generated output, binary
   176	files and vendored material may be excluded only through exact, documented
   177	policy. The check must cover Markdown and JSON as well as TypeScript, so it is
   178	not an Oxlint rule.
   179	
   180	The root README status-snapshot link must be repository-relative. Root
   181	verification must invoke the canonical path command so a future spec, plan or
   182	task list cannot reintroduce workstation-specific references.
   183	
   184	### 2. String-contract taxonomy
   185	
   186	Apply this taxonomy to exported, configured, persisted and provider-facing
   187	string-shaped values:
   188	
   189	- **Open semantic values** such as IDs, keys and opaque handles use an
   190	  owner-named checked string Schema plus `Schema.brand` when accidental mixing
   191	  is a real defect.
   192	- **Closed vocabularies** such as kinds, statuses, modes and operations use an
   193	  owner-named `Schema.Literal` or `Schema.Literals` contract and `Match` for
   194	  material branching.
   195	- **Secrets** use owner-named `Schema.Redacted` or
   196	  `Schema.RedactedFromValue`; a secret is not revealed merely to add a brand.
   197	- **Content** such as descriptions, messages and authored text uses an
   198	  owner-named checked Schema. Brand it only when two valid content domains
   199	  cross the same boundary and mixing them is a real defect.
   200	- **Transport primitives** such as serialized JSON, headers, URLs and process
   201	  output use named boundary Schemas when exported. Parser-local fragments may
   202	  remain local after their enclosing representation is decoded.
   203	- **Diagnostics** use safe checked text and must not contain secrets or raw
   204	  private payloads.
   205	
   206	Audit current contracts without mass renaming or mechanical branding. Reuse
   207	the owning Schema in consumers, decode the complete representation once at
   208	ingress, pass the canonical type inward and encode only at serialization
   209	egress. Any public package correction must include an appropriate Changeset.
   210	
   211	### 3. Portable Effect linting
   212	
   213	Compare current Effect rules with the live TaxKit codebase and admit only
   214	rules that can distinguish an architectural error from ordinary valid code.
   215	Initial candidates include bare `Effect.tryPromise`, host APIs in service
   216	contracts, Effect execution in adapters without an explicit boundary,
   217	nullable boundary leakage, manual `Result`/`Exit` re-encoding and non-throwing
   218	synchronous decoders outside their reviewed consumers.
   219	
   220	Existing calculator rules may move into the portable namespace only when the
   221	rule is domain-neutral and broader exact scopes are proven. Do not create a
   222	second decoder-placement rule or weaken the current exact allowlists. Do not
   223	add website- or route-specific rules in this rollout.
   224	
   225	Every admitted rule must resolve canonical imports and aliases, ignore
   226	unrelated shadowed locals, have focused visitor tests, and pass accepted and
   227	rejected fixtures through the installed Oxlint binary with nested config
   228	disabled. Fix real violations at their owning boundary; do not add broad
   229	ignores or suppressions to enable a rule.
   230	
   231	### 4. Production dependency graph
   232	
   233	Add a dedicated Knip production configuration and root
   234	`knip:production` command. Model actual public exports and executable
   235	entrypoints for the release-train packages, `@taxkit/scripts` commands and the
   236	standalone API runtime. Exclude tests, fixtures, examples, generated files and
   237	development-only tooling from production reachability.
   238	
   239	Resolve findings by correcting exports, entrypoints, imports or genuinely
   240	obsolete code. Exact exceptions require an ownership explanation; broad
   241	workspace ignores and development entrypoints must not be used to manufacture
   242	a passing graph. Keep the existing development-aware Knip command and run both
   243	graphs from root verification.
   244	
   245	## Tests and Verification
   246	
   247	- Each implementation slice must run `bun run verification` plus its focused
   248	  package, lint or Knip gates.
   249	- The path checker needs deterministic accepted/rejected fixtures and tests for
   250	  Markdown, JSON and source files, line reporting, exact exclusions and a
   251	  zero-findings repository run.
   252	- String-contract changes need owning-package type checks and tests, plus an
   253	  audit proving canonical schema/type reuse, one-time boundary decoding,
   254	  explicit egress encoding and no unsafe construction.
   255	- Every enabled portable lint rule needs visitor tests and real Oxlint binary
   256	  fixtures for accepted, rejected, aliased and unrelated-shadow cases.
   257	- The production Knip command must pass independently and as part of root
   258	  verification without relying on test or development entrypoints.
   259	- Substantial slices require three documented improvement audits covering
   260	  call graphs, ownership, Effect-native control flow, canonical contracts,
   261	  unsafe casts, DTO mirrors, stringly branching and helper sprawl.
   262	- No browser verification is required because current website applications are
   263	  explicitly outside this spec.
   264	
   265	## Risks and Tradeoffs
   266	
   267	- A path rule can reject legitimate prose if its pattern is too broad. Exact
   268	  fixtures and tracked-text policy are required before enabling it globally.
   269	- String-contract audits can create noisy nominal types. The taxonomy requires
   270	  a concrete mixing risk or boundary contract and explicitly rejects branding
   271	  by default.
   272	- Over-broad linting creates suppression culture. Rules without reliable
   273	  static evidence remain documented review guidance.
   274	- A production Knip graph can miss framework-discovered entrypoints or flag
   275	  legitimate conditional exports. Every exception must be exact and tied to a
   276	  real runtime owner.
   277	- The current website apps remain outside the production graph and will need a
   278	  separate decision if either implementation survives future replacement.
   279	
   280	## Versioning and Changelog Impact
   281	
   282	Path checking, lint tooling, root verification and production Knip
   283	configuration are repository-internal and do not require Changesets unless
   284	their implementation changes a publishable package contract or behavior.
   285	
   286	String-contract corrections that alter public package schemas, exports,
   287	accepted inputs, encoded outputs or observable errors require package-owned
   288	Changesets. Internal-only type tightening or documentation updates must record
   289	an explicit no-Changeset rationale.
   290	
   291	Do not run `bun run version-repo` as part of this work.
   292	
   293	## Acceptance Criteria
   294	
   295	- Canonical root verification reports zero tracked machine-local checkout
   296	  references and prevents their recurrence.
   297	- The current 33-reference baseline is removed without deleting useful
   298	  repository-relative history.
   299	- Canonical architecture or standards guidance defines the six string-contract
   300	  categories and current public/config/persistence contracts have been audited
   301	  against them.
   302	- Consumers reuse owner-named schemas and derived types; the final diff contains
   303	  no generic brand factory, mirrored DTOs, repeated internal decoding or unsafe
   304	  brand casts.
   305	- Every newly enabled portable Effect rule has an exact scope, binding-aware
   306	  tests and accepted/rejected real-binary evidence.
   307	- Existing decoder, route-transport, tax-specific and browser/server import
   308	  boundaries remain at least as strict as before.
   309	- `bun run knip` and `bun run knip:production` both pass, and the production
   310	  graph covers release packages, repository commands and `apps/api` without
   311	  test or development reachability.
   312	- `bun run verification`, `bun run test`, `bun run build` and
   313	  `bun run release:check` pass after all slices.
   314	- Each task's Changeset or no-Changeset decision is reviewed before commit.
   315	- The final implementation and architecture docs still match the target call
   316	  graphs in this spec.

     7	
     8	# Scripts
     9	
    10	`@taxkit/scripts` owns cross-cutting repository command orchestration. Its
    11	implemented release-readiness command runs the existing verification and
    12	package-owned release gates as one ordered, typed Effect program.
    13	
    14	## Ownership
    15	
    16	This package owns:
    17	
    18	- schema-backed release check definitions, command outcomes and the final
    19	  readiness report
    20	- the `ReleaseCommandRunner` service contract
    21	- the Effect Platform child-process live layer and deterministic test layer
    22	- the release-readiness program, rendering policy and Bun runtime entrypoint
    23	
    24	It does not own the validators it invokes. SDK packing and downstream checks
    25	stay in `packages/sdk/typescript`, docs validation and browser proof stay with
    26	the docs packages/app, API smoke stays in `apps/api`, and Changesets, Turbo,
    27	lint, tests and builds remain behind their canonical root or package commands.
    28	
    29	## Command
    30	
    31	From the repository root, run:
    32	
    33	```sh
    34	bun run release:check
    35	```
    36	
    37	The command runs these checks sequentially and stops after the first typed
    38	failure:
    39	
    40	1. `bun run verification`
    41	2. `bun run test`
    42	3. `bun run build`
    43	4. `bun run docs:validate`
    44	5. `bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact`
    45	6. `bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream`
    46	7. `bun run --filter=api smoke`
    47	8. `bun run --filter=docs test:browser`
    48	9. `bun run changeset status --verbose`
    49	
    50	Each invocation records its exact executable, arguments, working directory,
    51	exit code, standard output and standard error in a schema-backed outcome.
    52	Non-zero exits become `ReleaseCheckFailedError`; Effect Platform execution
    53	failures become `ReleaseCommandExecutionError`.
    54	
    55	## Runtime Shape
    56	
    57	```text
    58	root release:check
    59	  -> package release:check
    60	  -> BunRuntime entrypoint
    61	  -> BunServices.layer
    62	     -> Path.fromFileUrl -> workspace root
    63	     -> ReleaseCommandRunnerLive -> ChildProcessSpawner
    64	  -> runReleaseReadiness -> ReleaseCommandRunner
    65	  -> ChildProcess Command
    66	  -> existing root and package-owned commands
    67	```
    68	
    69	`runReleaseReadiness` is the primary linear Effect program. The service
    70	contract and live layer depend only on the Effect `ChildProcessSpawner`
    71	capability. The Bun runtime entrypoint resolves the repository root with
    72	`Path.fromFileUrl`, composes `BunServices.layer`, and is the only place that
    73	provides the host implementation or executes the completed Effect.
    74	
    75	## Testing
    76	
    77	```sh
    78	bun run --filter=@taxkit/scripts test
    79	bun run --filter=@taxkit/scripts check-types
    80	bun run --filter=@taxkit/scripts build
    81	```
    82	
    83	The deterministic layer uses `HashMap` and `Ref` to record invocations without
    84	starting processes. Tests prove command order, exact arguments and working
    85	directory, schema-backed outcomes, non-zero failure policy, process failures,
    86	fail-fast behavior and success/failure rendering.
    87	
    88	## Guardrails
    89	
    90	- Add orchestration only when a workflow genuinely crosses package owners.
    91	- Record the abstraction-admission evidence for each new cross-owner workflow:
    92	  owner, semantic policy, consumers or substitution, simpler graph and focused
    93	  tests.
    94	- Invoke canonical commands; do not copy their validation logic into this
    95	  package.
    96	- Keep one primary linear Effect program and one runtime execution boundary.
    97	- Keep command failures tagged and outcomes schema-backed.
    98	- Add a Changeset for package-facing command or contract changes.
    99	- Do not import this package into browser-safe SDK, calculator, rule or engine
   100	  entrypoints.
   101

   215	
   216	Treat a TanStack Start server-function call and TanStack Router loader-state

     8	# Package ownership
     9	
    10	Package ownership defines where new TaxKit code should belong as the repo
    11	grows and which package will be allowed to define canonical contracts. It does
    12	not imply that every named package exists today.
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	This doc routes ownership decisions. [Package boundaries](./package-boundaries.md)
    17	contains the proposed package map and dependency direction.
    18	
    19	Current implemented code lives in:
    20	
    21	- `apps/api`
    22	- `apps/docs`
    23	- `apps/web`
    24	- `packages/core`
    25	- `packages/calculators`
    26	- `packages/docs-content`
    27	- `packages/docs-fumadocs`
    28	- `packages/api/http`
    29	- `packages/sdk/typescript`
    30	- `packages/rules/au/income-tax`
    31	- `packages/rules/au/pay`
    32	- `packages/rules/au/stsl`
    33	- `packages/scripts`
    34	- `packages/testing`
    35	- `packages/tsconfig`
    36	
    37	Current planned ownership placeholder:
    38	
    39	- `packages/ui`
    40	
    41	The placeholder directories contain README guidance only. Do not route runtime
    42	imports, source ownership or build expectations to them until package manifests
    43	and source exports exist.
    44	
    45	## Main areas
    46	
    47	`packages/core`
    48	: Implemented shared primitives, fact descriptors, rule descriptors, graph
    49	metadata, trace and ledger contracts, common tagged errors and calculation
    50	engine service.
    51	
    52	`packages/domain/au/*`
    53	: Planned Australian date dimensions and domain facts that are not owned by a
    54	single rule pack.
    55	
    56	`packages/rules/au/*`
    57	: Official Australian rule packs, parameter tables, algorithms, source
    58	references, graph metadata, rule-owned calculator ids/context literals and
    59	golden tests. Current implemented packages are `pay`, `income-tax` and `stsl`.
    60	
    61	`packages/testing`
    62	: Shared test helpers for workspace packages. It must not become a back door
    63	for production-only runtime helpers.
    64	
    65	`packages/scripts`
    66	: Implemented private repository-automation package. It owns schema-backed,
    67	  Effect-native orchestration that crosses package owners, including the
    68	  release-readiness command, its command-runner service, live process layer,
    69	  deterministic test layer and runtime entrypoint. It invokes canonical root
    70	  and package commands without moving or duplicating their validator logic.
    71	
    72	`packages/api/http`
    73	: Implemented HTTP API package. It owns Effect HTTP API definitions, boundary
    74	schemas, thin server handlers, OpenAPI, typed HTTP clients and HTTP
    75	status/transport annotations.
    76	
    77	`packages/calculators`
    78	: Implemented reusable calculator orchestration package. It owns calculator
    79	catalog composition schemas, calculator service methods, metadata projections,
    80	graph response construction, schema-guided error shaping and
    81	rule-pack/scenario composition used by HTTP, SDK, CLI and in-process callers.
    82	It also owns the canonical reusable calculator run schemas named
    83	`CalculatorRun*` and the `CalculatorServiceError` union. HTTP-only public
    84	envelopes and status annotations stay in `packages/api/http`; SDK schema
    85	exports may re-export calculator-owned run contracts but must not duplicate
    86	them. It depends on `packages/core` and rule packages, but it must not depend
    87	on HTTP handlers, SDK clients, CLI commands or app runtime modules.
    88	
    89	`packages/sdk/typescript`
    90	: Implemented private TypeScript SDK package for a future public SDK
    91	publication. It owns browser-safe schemas, typed calculation facades,
    92	Effect-native subpaths, jurisdiction modules, examples, compatibility tests and
    93	packed-artifact checks. Its strict downstream validator may orchestrate the
    94	nine-package release closure and materialize package-declared publication
    95	exports in temporary tarballs, but package manifests and exports remain owned
    96	by their packages. It must not depend on `@taxkit/api-http`; HTTP
    97	transports consume the SDK rather than the reverse. Its Effect entrypoint owns
    98	request-preserving calculator helpers such as `calculateRunRequest`,
    99	`calculateReportRequest` and `calculateReport`, while reusing
   100	calculator-owned `CalculatorRun*` schemas and `CalculatorServiceError`.
   101	
   102	`apps/web`
   103	: Current scaffold app. It proves the runtime boundary and health endpoint
   104	while a future product workflow is still unscoped.
   105	
   106	`apps/docs`
   107	: Implemented public documentation app. It owns TanStack Start routes, the
   108	  docs app shell, route loaders, search/navigation presentation and app-local
   109	  MDX component composition. It consumes package-owned content and Fumadocs
   110	  helpers, but does not own canonical frontmatter, navigation, generated source
   111	  or reusable Fumadocs integration contracts.
   112	
   113	`apps/api`
   114	: Current standalone Bun API runtime. It owns process config, startup,
   115	shutdown and platform serving for the implemented API app.
   116	
   117	`packages/docs-content`
   118	: Implemented private source-only content package. It owns TaxKit docs
   119	  frontmatter, meta, navigation, validation issues, tagged docs errors,
   120	  `DocsContentService`, the Fumadocs `source.config.ts` for
   121	  `apps/docs/content` and the generated `.source/*` boundary. It can read raw
   122	  MDX source text for validation policy, but app routes should use its service
   123	  and client exports instead of importing source files directly.
   124	
   125	`packages/docs-fumadocs`
   126	: Implemented private reusable package for generic Fumadocs integration. It
   127	  owns Effect Schema to Standard Schema bridging, shared MDX compile config,
   128	  source-loader adapters, page-tree helpers and generic browser-safe MDX render
   129	  primitives. It must not own TaxKit-specific frontmatter, navigation,
   130	  validation policy, routes or generated content.
   131	
   132	## Runtime shape
   133	
   134	Engine packages should be deterministic and reusable. Runtime-specific code
   135	belongs in apps or explicitly server-only package exports.
   136	
   137	## Guardrails
   138	
   139	- Define canonical schemas in the owning package.
   140	- Owning packages define canonical schemas, schema-derived types, branded ids,
   141	  constructors, service tags and tagged errors. Non-owners may adapt unknown
   142	  inputs at boundaries, but MUST import the canonical contracts instead of
   143	  redeclaring object shapes or fields such as `id: string`.
   144	- Define reusable config schemas in the package that owns the runtime contract,
   145	  then compose and provide them from app-specific config modules.
   146	- Import from the owner instead of redefining boundary values locally.
   147	- Add server-only exports for filesystem, HTTP server and Node adapters.
   148	- Keep React in apps or docs packages only.
   149	- Keep cross-package command orchestration in `packages/scripts`, but keep each
   150	  validator and its domain policy with the package or app it validates.
   151	- Keep app-specific MDX components in `apps/docs`; promote only generic,
   152	  repeated Fumadocs primitives to `packages/docs-fumadocs/render` or repeated
   153	  TaxKit UI primitives to `packages/ui`.
   154	- Do not add flat engine packages once nested domain or rule ownership exists.
   155	  `packages/calculators` is allowed because it is a cross-surface
   156	  orchestration package rather than a jurisdiction/domain/rule package.
   157	- Keep HTTP handlers thin. Transport handlers may extract route parameters and
   158	  call package-owned services, but reusable calculator lookup, metadata
   159	  transformation, graph assembly, calculation dispatch and expected error
   160	  shaping belong in service packages such as `packages/calculators`. The
   161	  current calculate handler is thinner still: it selects the SDK descriptor for
   162	  the route calculator id, calls `@taxkit/sdk/effect` `calculateRunRequest`
   163	  once, and maps only transport envelopes.
   164	
   165	## Related docs
   166	
   167	- [Package boundaries](./package-boundaries.md)
   168	- [Effect services](./effect-services.md)
   169	- [API and SDK](./api-and-sdk.md)

     1	# Versioning And Changesets
     2	
     3	TaxKit uses Changesets to manage package versions and package changelogs.
     4	Public apps can also maintain curated app-level changelogs for public
     5	contracts, deployments and operational changes that are meaningful outside npm
     6	package installation. The root `CHANGELOG.md` is the curated release-train
     7	changelog for humans reading the repository as one product.
     8	
     9	## Release Train Policy
    10	
    11	All `@taxkit/*` packages are in one fixed version group:
    12	
    13	- `@taxkit/core`
    14	- `@taxkit/api-http`
    15	- `@taxkit/rules-au-income-tax`
    16	- `@taxkit/rules-au-pay`
    17	- `@taxkit/rules-au-stsl`
    18	- `@taxkit/sdk`
    19	- `@taxkit/testing`
    20	- `@taxkit/tsconfig`
    21	
    22	When any package in this group is released, every package in the group receives
    23	the same version. This follows the Effect-style release train model: packages
    24	are tested, documented, and consumed as one compatible set.
    25	
    26	Apps are not part of the package release train and do not have independently
    27	managed npm package versions. Public apps can still maintain app-level
    28	changelogs. `apps/api/CHANGELOG.md` tracks public HTTP API contract and
    29	deployment-facing changes.
    30	
    31	## Changeset Config
    32	
    33	The repository config lives in `.changeset/config.json`.
    34	
    35	Important settings:
    36	
    37	- `fixed`: keeps all `@taxkit/*` packages on the same version.
    38	- `privatePackages.version: true`: package versions are managed even while
    39	  packages remain `private: true`.
    40	- `privatePackages.tag: true`: release tags can still be created for private
    41	  package versions.
    42	- `access: "public"`: future npm publication for scoped packages should be
    43	  public by default once package `private` flags are removed.
    44	- `bumpVersionsWithWorkspaceProtocolOnly: true`: internal dependency ranges are
    45	  only rewritten where workspace protocol is used.
    46	
    47	## Commands
    48	
    49	Create a changeset for package-facing work:
    50	
    51	```sh
    52	bun run changeset
    53	```
    54	
    55	Apply pending changesets to package versions and changelogs:
    56	
    57	```sh
    58	bun run version-repo
    59	```
    60	
    61	Inspect pending releases without modifying files:
    62	
    63	```sh
    64	bun run changeset status --verbose
    65	```
    66	
    67	## Rules
    68	
    69	- Every package-facing API, behavior, tooling or public documentation change
    70	  needs a changeset.
    71	- Use the highest required semver bump across the release train.
    72	- Keep changeset summaries user-facing; describe the public effect of the
    73	  change, not the implementation mechanics only.
    74	- Do not manually edit package versions during normal work. Let
    75	  `bun run version-repo` consume changesets and update versions together.
    76	- Use `bun run version-repo` in a dedicated versioning commit or release-prep
    77	  slice. Normal implementation commits should add changesets, not consume them,
    78	  unless the user explicitly asks to version the repo.
    79	- After `bun run version-repo`, update the root `CHANGELOG.md` in the same
    80	  release-prep slice with a concise release-train summary and links to the
    81	  package changelogs generated by Changesets.
    82	- For public API-facing changes, update `apps/api/CHANGELOG.md` in the same
    83	  slice. Treat it as the public HTTP API contract/deployment changelog, not a
    84	  Changesets-generated package changelog.
    85	- Public docs and specs are versioned too when they affect package behavior,
    86	  API behavior, install guidance, route design or generated documentation.
    87	  Docs-only typo fixes can use an explicit no-changeset rationale.
    88	- Keep package `private: true` until the package is ready for npm publication.
    89	  Changesets still manages versions while packages are private.
    55	     -> consumer-only file overrides resolve unpublished internal packages
    56	  -> bun install
    57	  -> TypeScript typecheck with a negative misuse assertion
    58	  -> run plain and Effect SDK calculations

    60	  -> browser-bundle root, AU and schemas SDK entrypoints
    61	  -> print artifact counts and command evidence

    76	
    77	## Publication surface
    78	
    79	Compiled package builds remove `dist` before `tsc`. Workspace manifests may
    80	retain `source` export conditions for local development. Their `files` fields
    81	limit artifacts, while `publishConfig.exports` owns the dist-only publication
    82	view.
    83	
    84	Bun 1.3.14 resolves workspace and catalogue dependency protocols during
    85	`bun pm pack`, but it does not replace top-level exports with
    86	`publishConfig.exports`. The strict validator therefore stages the actual Bun
    87	tarball, materializes the declared publication export map with structured
    88	manifest APIs, and Bun-packs that staged package again. The final tarball, not
    89	the workspace directory or a dry-run file list, is the validation subject.
    90	
   155

   158	package without an explicit release-prep approval.
   159	
   160	### Downstream validation
   161	
   162	The SDK owns the first downstream consumer validation gate:
   163	
   164	```sh
   165	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
   166	```
   167	
   168	The command builds and Bun-packs the nine-package release closure, materializes
   169	each package's dist-only `publishConfig.exports` in a staged tarball, and
   170	rejects source files, missing export targets or unresolved `workspace:*` and
   171	`catalog:` ranges. It installs all unpublished tarballs into a temporary
   172	consumer outside the repo, typechecks and runs SDK examples, imports every
   173	JavaScript public entrypoint and bundles the browser-safe SDK surface.
   174	
   175	The command is always strict. Consumer-only file overrides connect unpublished
   176	internal tarballs without changing their concrete registry-ready dependency
   177	ranges. Any manifest or consumer regression prints evidence and exits nonzero;

     4	source_of_truth: docs
     5	confidence: high
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Testing and quality
     9	
    10	TaxKit quality depends on deterministic calculation tests, package boundary
    11	tests, graph validation, trace snapshots, API/SDK parity and build/type health.
    12	
    13	## Scope
    14	
    15	This doc owns cross-cutting quality expectations. Detailed rule-package test
    16	requirements live in [Testing and validation](./testing-and-validation.md).
    17	
    18	## Main areas
    19	
    20	- rule-builder unit tests
    21	- ATO golden tests and known scenarios
    22	- property tests for thresholds and monotonicity
    23	- date-boundary tests
    24	- graph validation in CI
    25	- trace snapshots
    26	- package export and browser-safety tests
    27	- API and SDK parity tests
    28	
    29	## Current baseline
    30	
    31	The current repository baseline is canonical root verification:
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	bun run verification
    35	```
    36	
    37	Root verification includes lint, format, Knip and workspace type checks. For
    38	docs, that means `apps/docs` type checking also typechecks checked examples,
    39	and dependent package builds run before type checks through Turbo. Heavier
    40	docs runtime gates remain explicit package commands so normal local
    41	verification does not rebuild and validate the whole docs corpus on every
    42	change:
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	bun run docs:validate
    46	bun run docs:build
    47	bun run --filter=docs test:browser
    48	bun run --filter=@taxkit/docs-content test
    49	```
    50	
    51	Run those package-local docs gates whenever MDX content, Fumadocs source
    52	wiring, docs examples, validation policy or docs rendering changes.
    53	
    54	Release-facing package work must also prove actual tarballs rather than
    55	workspace imports or dry-run file lists:
    56	
    57	```bash
    58	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact
    59	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
    60	```
    61	
    62	The focused command uses an Effect-native, scope-managed Bun runtime to pack,
    63	inspect and import the SDK artifact. The strict command builds the nine-package
    64	release closure, materializes each declared dist-only
    65	`publishConfig.exports` view, Bun-packs it, rejects source/protocol leakage,
    66	installs all tarballs in a clean external workspace, typechecks and runs SDK
    67	examples, imports every JavaScript public entrypoint and browser-bundles the
    68	browser-safe SDK surface. It has no audit-only success mode.
    69	
    70	The docs browser command runs a programmatic client-side TanStack route harness
    71	in Chromium. It may prove direct `Route.useLoaderData` restoration, recoverable
    72	route UI, framework error boundaries and console cleanliness, but it does not
    73	prove SSR or hydration. Prove initial SSR, hydration and client navigation
    74	separately against the built app on `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`, including
    75	a successful server-function response and no document request during the client
    76	transition.
    77	
    78	Public API route work should also capture contract evidence from the standalone
    79	API app:
    80	
    81	- generated OpenAPI route evidence from `/api/docs/openapi.json`
    82	- at least one metadata route smoke check
    83	- at least one successful calculation route smoke check
    84	- at least one schema-guided error response with field paths and descriptor
    85	  help
    86	- Changeset status evidence for package-facing changes
    87	
    88	The implemented release-readiness command composes the complete local release
    89	evidence without taking ownership of those validators:
    90	
    91	```bash
    92	bun run release:check
    93	```
    94	
    95	`@taxkit/scripts` runs root verification, workspace tests and builds, docs
    96	content validation, the focused SDK artifact check, strict downstream package
    97	validation, API smoke, docs browser proof and Changeset status in that order.
    98	The command uses the Effect Platform child-process `Command` model through a
    99	`ReleaseCommandRunner` service, records schema-backed outcomes, and fails fast
   100	with tagged execution or non-zero-exit errors. Package-owned command
   101	implementations remain in their current packages and apps. The live runner
   102	depends on `ChildProcessSpawner`; only the Bun runtime entrypoint provides
   103	`BunServices.layer`, and that same runtime resolves the workspace root through
   104	Effect `Path.fromFileUrl`.
   105	
   106	```text
   107	root release:check
   108	  -> @taxkit/scripts runtime
   109	  -> ReleaseCommandRunner
   110	  -> canonical root, app and package commands
   111	  -> schema-backed ordered outcomes or one tagged failure
   112	```
   113	
   114	`release:check` is the complete local release-evidence graph, not publication
   115	approval. Versioning, changelog application and publishing remain explicit
   116	operations after a human reviews pending Changesets and the release impact.
   117	
   118	## Review evidence
   119	
   120	Substantial code, package-boundary, API, SDK, app-runtime or documentation
   121	rollouts record three audit passes in their task evidence or execution plan:
   122	
   123	1. Compare the final code and command graphs with their owning architecture and
   124	   spec.
   125	2. Inspect Effect flow, schemas, tagged errors, unsafe casts, DTO mirrors and
   126	   helper or abstraction sprawl.
   127	3. Inspect CI, lint, packed-consumer, browser/API, documentation and Changeset
   128	   evidence appropriate to the changed surface.
   129	
   130	New shared abstractions must satisfy the
   131	[abstraction admission contract](../design-docs/abstraction-admission.md).
   132	Focused tests must prove the claimed policy or substitution point; coverage
   133	that only calls through a wrapper is not admission evidence. Static lint is a
   134	supporting gate and cannot replace semantic ownership or call-graph review.
   135	
   136	## Guardrails
   137	
   138	- A rule pack is incomplete without source references and golden tests.
   139	- Graph validation failures should fail the build.
   140	- API responses must stay schema-backed.
   141	- Public docs content must validate through `@taxkit/docs-content` before
   142	  documentation/runtime slices are accepted.
   143	- Keep browser tooling in app dev dependencies and browser harness routes out
   144	  of production route trees.
   145	- Browser-safe exports must not import Node-only modules.
   146	- Oxlint can enforce restricted APIs, such as banned `Object.*` enumeration
   147	  helpers, but it does not currently provide a safe built-in rule for banning
   148	  functions below a minimum line count. Prefer review and architecture guidance
   149	  for tiny one-off wrapper or mapper helpers.
   150	- `tools/oxlint/effect-rules.js`, `bun-rules.js` and `mdx-rules.js` own
   151	  domain-neutral contracts. `taxkit-rules.js` owns tax/calculator policy plus
   152	  decoder and route-transport rules. Do not put package names or tax defaults
   153	  into a portable rule message.
   154	- Portable Effect rules ban manual `_tag` literals and `switch`, keep live/test
   155	  Layers out of service contracts, restrict encoder execution, reject throwing
   156	  Schema sync codecs, preserve typed service errors and tagged-error causes,
   157	  and keep runtime, console, process and host imports at configured boundaries.
   158	  Use `Data`/`Schema` tagged classes, `Match`, Effect Platform services and
   159	  exact live/runtime adapters instead. Binding-sensitive rules resolve
   160	  canonical and namespace imports, renamed bindings, aliases and statically
   161	  known destructuring. Accepted real-binary fixtures prove that unrelated
   162	  shadowed locals with the same names do not report.
   163	- Bun rules keep `Bun.file`, `Bun.write`, `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.serve` and
   164	  `BunRuntime.runMain` in exact adapter/entrypoint files. The MDX rule keeps
   165	  route-local component registries out of route composition. The test-global
   166	  rule rejects split ownership of unaliased `describe`, `expect`, `it` or
   167	  `test` between `@effect/vitest` and `vitest`. Vitest-only utilities such as
   168	  `vi` or hooks may be imported beside `@effect/vitest`; an explicitly aliased
   169	  secondary shared API is also valid.
   170	- Calculator service code under `packages/calculators/src` has stricter custom
   171	  Oxlint rules that ban raw `typeof`, `instanceof`, `in`, `=== undefined`,
   172	  conditional object-spread shaping and jurisdiction/tax-year `??` defaults.
   173	  These rules enforce Schema, Option, Match and schema-owned optional fields for
   174	  public calculator policy. The same scope also bans raw `null` comparison,
   175	  nested wrapper-call composition, native array pipelines, native `Map`/`Set`,
   176	  thrown exceptions, `async`/`await`/`new Promise`, ad hoc
   177	  `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` and hidden time/randomness so calculator
   178	  services use pipe-first composition, Effect `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashMap`,
   179	  `HashSet`, `Effect`, `Layer`, `Clock`, `Random` and schema codecs instead of
   180	  vanilla JavaScript/TypeScript escape hatches.

    95	verification` is the baseline verification command for documentation, package
    96	wiring and scaffold changes. `bun run release:check` runs the complete ordered
    97	release evidence, including tests, builds, package artifacts, API smoke, docs
    98	browser proof and Changeset status.
    99

   124	  material.

   126	## Status snapshot
   127	
   128	[docs/repo-status-outline.html](./docs/repo-status-outline.html) is a local,
   129	static status snapshot for a quick visual overview. It is useful for review in a
   130	browser, but it is not canonical; refresh it when repo structure or implemented

   138	
   139	## Runtime boundary
   140	
   141	- `apps/api` is the API runtime owner. It creates one process-lifetime
   142	  `ManagedRuntime`, serves `packages/api/http` through Bun and disposes scoped
   143	  resources on shutdown.
   144	- `apps/docs` is the docs runtime owner. It consumes `@taxkit/docs-content`
   145	  and `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` rather than owning canonical frontmatter,
   146	  navigation or reusable Fumadocs internals.
   147	- `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts` and
   148	  `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts` own the web SSR and browser client
   149	  runtimes. They call the standalone API over HTTP.
   150	- `@taxkit/api-http/client` and `@taxkit/api-http/client/live` are
   151	  browser-safe.
   152	- `@taxkit/api-http/client/server`, `@taxkit/api-http/server` and handler
   153	  exports are server-only and should stay out of `apps/web`.
    29	## Current baseline
    30	
    31	The current repository baseline is canonical root verification:
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	bun run verification
    35	```
    36	
    37	Root verification includes lint, format, Knip and workspace type checks. For
    38	docs, that means `apps/docs` type checking also typechecks checked examples,
    39	and dependent package builds run before type checks through Turbo. Heavier
    40	docs runtime gates remain explicit package commands so normal local
    41	verification does not rebuild and validate the whole docs corpus on every
    42	change:
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	bun run docs:validate
    46	bun run docs:build
    47	bun run --filter=docs test:browser
    48	bun run --filter=@taxkit/docs-content test
    49	```
    50	
    51	Run those package-local docs gates whenever MDX content, Fumadocs source
    52	wiring, docs examples, validation policy or docs rendering changes.
    53	
    54	Release-facing package work must also prove actual tarballs rather than
    55	workspace imports or dry-run file lists:
    56	
    57	```bash
    58	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact
    59	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
    60	```
    61	
    62	The focused command uses an Effect-native, scope-managed Bun runtime to pack,
    63	inspect and import the SDK artifact. The strict command builds the nine-package
    64	release closure, materializes each declared dist-only
    65	`publishConfig.exports` view, Bun-packs it, rejects source/protocol leakage,
    66	installs all tarballs in a clean external workspace, typechecks and runs SDK
    67	examples, imports every JavaScript public entrypoint and browser-bundles the
    68	browser-safe SDK surface. It has no audit-only success mode.
    69	
    70	The docs browser command runs a programmatic client-side TanStack route harness
    71	in Chromium. It may prove direct `Route.useLoaderData` restoration, recoverable
    72	route UI, framework error boundaries and console cleanliness, but it does not
    73	prove SSR or hydration. Prove initial SSR, hydration and client navigation
    74	separately against the built app on `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`, including
    75	a successful server-function response and no document request during the client
    76	transition.
    77	
    78	Public API route work should also capture contract evidence from the standalone
    79	API app:
    80	
    81	- generated OpenAPI route evidence from `/api/docs/openapi.json`
    82	- at least one metadata route smoke check
    83	- at least one successful calculation route smoke check
    84	- at least one schema-guided error response with field paths and descriptor
    85	  help
    86	- Changeset status evidence for package-facing changes
    87	
    88	The implemented release-readiness command composes the complete local release
    89	evidence without taking ownership of those validators:
    90	
    91	```bash
    92	bun run release:check
    93	```
    94	
    95	`@taxkit/scripts` runs root verification, workspace tests and builds, docs
    96	content validation, the focused SDK artifact check, strict downstream package
    97	validation, API smoke, docs browser proof and Changeset status in that order.
    98	The command uses the Effect Platform child-process `Command` model through a
    99	`ReleaseCommandRunner` service, records schema-backed outcomes, and fails fast
   100	with tagged execution or non-zero-exit errors. Package-owned command
   101	implementations remain in their current packages and apps. The live runner
   102	depends on `ChildProcessSpawner`; only the Bun runtime entrypoint provides
   103	`BunServices.layer`, and that same runtime resolves the workspace root through
   104	Effect `Path.fromFileUrl`.
   105	
   106	```text
   107	root release:check
   108	  -> @taxkit/scripts runtime
   109	  -> ReleaseCommandRunner
   110	  -> canonical root, app and package commands
   111	  -> schema-backed ordered outcomes or one tagged failure
   112	```
   113	
   114	`release:check` is the complete local release-evidence graph, not publication
   115	approval. Versioning, changelog application and publishing remain explicit
   116	operations after a human reviews pending Changesets and the release impact.
   117	
   118	## Review evidence
   119	
   120	Substantial code, package-boundary, API, SDK, app-runtime or documentation
    61	`packages/testing`
    62	: Shared test helpers for workspace packages. It must not become a back door
    63	for production-only runtime helpers.

    66	: Implemented private repository-automation package. It owns schema-backed,
    67	  Effect-native orchestration that crosses package owners, including the
    68	  release-readiness command, its command-runner service, live process layer,
    69	  deterministic test layer and runtime entrypoint. It invokes canonical root
    70	  and package commands without moving or duplicating their validator logic.

   137	## Guardrails
   138	
   139	- Define canonical schemas in the owning package.
   140	- Owning packages define canonical schemas, schema-derived types, branded ids,
   141	  constructors, service tags and tagged errors. Non-owners may adapt unknown
   142	  inputs at boundaries, but MUST import the canonical contracts instead of
   143	  redeclaring object shapes or fields such as `id: string`.
   144	- Define reusable config schemas in the package that owns the runtime contract,
   145	  then compose and provide them from app-specific config modules.
   146	- Import from the owner instead of redefining boundary values locally.
   147	- Add server-only exports for filesystem, HTTP server and Node adapters.
   148	- Keep React in apps or docs packages only.
   149	- Keep cross-package command orchestration in `packages/scripts`, but keep each
   150	  validator and its domain policy with the package or app it validates.
   151	- Keep app-specific MDX components in `apps/docs`; promote only generic,
   152	  repeated Fumadocs primitives to `packages/docs-fumadocs/render` or repeated
   153	  TaxKit UI primitives to `packages/ui`.
   154	- Do not add flat engine packages once nested domain or rule ownership exists.
     8	# Scripts
     9	
    10	`@taxkit/scripts` owns cross-cutting repository command orchestration. Its
    11	implemented release-readiness command runs the existing verification and
    12	package-owned release gates as one ordered, typed Effect program.
    13	
    14	## Ownership
    15	
    16	This package owns:
    17	
    18	- schema-backed release check definitions, command outcomes and the final
    19	  readiness report
    20	- the `ReleaseCommandRunner` service contract
    21	- the Effect Platform child-process live layer and deterministic test layer
    22	- the release-readiness program, rendering policy and Bun runtime entrypoint
    23	
    24	It does not own the validators it invokes. SDK packing and downstream checks
    25	stay in `packages/sdk/typescript`, docs validation and browser proof stay with
    26	the docs packages/app, API smoke stays in `apps/api`, and Changesets, Turbo,
    27	lint, tests and builds remain behind their canonical root or package commands.
